examples: The big puzzle is a challenge.
Tying my shoes was a challenge.
This game is a fun challenge.

more.def: Something difficult that tests your skill or strength.
examples: Climbing the steep hill was a real challenge.
Learning a new language can be a challenge.
The long math problem was a challenge for the whole class.

easy.def: A time when you can do something.
examples: I got a chance to play.
This is your chance.
She wants a chance.

more.def: A time or situation that lets you do something you want.
examples: I got a chance to hold a baby chick at the farm.
This is your chance to ask the scientist a question.
Give the new student a chance to join the game.
There is a chance of rain.
No chance of snow.
He has a good chance.

more.def: How likely it is that something will happen.
examples: There is a chance of thunder this afternoon.
Our team has a good chance of winning the game.
The chance of seeing a whale today is small.

easy.def: To become different, or to make different.
examples: Leaves change color.
I changed my shirt.
The weather changes.

more.def: To become different, or to make something different.
examples: Tadpoles change into frogs as they grow.
She changed her clothes after playing in the mud.
The traffic light changed from red to green.
The change was big.
We need a change.
I like this change.

more.def: The act of becoming different, or the result of that.
examples: The change from summer to fall is my favorite time of year.
Moving to a new school was a big change for her.
A change of plans meant we stayed home.

easy.def: Coins that you get back or have in your pocket.
examples: I have change.
She got change back.
He saved his change.

more.def: The coins you get back when you pay with more than the cost, or small coins in general.
examples: The cashier gave me change after I paid with a ten-dollar bill.
I found some change in the couch cushions.
He kept his change in a small jar.

easy.def: To ask someone to pay money.
examples: The shop charges two dollars for juice.
The bus charges a dollar for kids.
They charged us nothing.

more.def: To ask a certain amount of money for something.
examples: The farm charges five dollars to pick a basket of berries.
The museum does not charge children under five.
How much do they charge for a pony ride?

easy.def: To put power into a battery.
examples: I charge my tablet each night.
The toy car needs to be charged.
Mom charged the battery.

more.def: To fill a battery with electricity so it can work.
examples: Plug in the tablet to charge the battery.
The electric car charges overnight in the garage.
My watch charges in about an hour.
The kids charged out of the door.
The puppy charged across the yard.
He charged down the hill on his sled.
The kids charged out the door when the bell rang.
The puppy charged across the yard to greet us.
A rhino can charge at high speed when it is startled.

easy.def: The job of looking after something.
examples: Maya is in charge of the plants.
The teacher is in charge of the class.
Who is in charge here?

more.def: The responsibility for looking after or leading something.
examples: Our coach put Dani in charge of the water bottles.
The captain is in charge of the whole ship.
Who is in charge of the library today?

easy.def: To look to see if something is right.
examples: I check my work.
She checked the door.
Check the time.

more.def: To look at something to make sure it is correct, safe, or working.
examples: Please check your answers before you hand in the test.
Dad checked the tires before the long drive.
The nurse checked my ears and my throat.
She has a cheerful smile.
The room is painted a cheerful yellow.
A cheerful bird sang to us.

more.def: Happy and full of good feelings.
examples: The cheerful bus driver greeted every child by name.
He stayed cheerful even though it rained on his birthday.
The nurse's cheerful voice made the patients feel better.
The child ran to the park.
Each child gets a book.
A child is small and young.

more.def: A young person who is not yet an adult.
examples: Every child in the class got a turn on the swing.
The child found a tiny frog under a rock.
Museums often have special programs for each child.
Grandma has three children.
Their child is in my class.
She is their only child.

more.def: A person's son or daughter, no matter how old they are.
examples: My grandmother's children are my mom and my two uncles.
Even as an adult, she is still her parents' child.
The bear led her two children across the stream.
It was a hard choice.
You have a choice of two toys.
Make your choice.

more.def: The act of picking one thing from two or more things.
examples: It was a hard choice between the red and blue shirts.
You have a choice of milk or juice.
Her choice was to take the shorter path.

easy.def: A holiday on December 25 when many people give gifts.
examples: We decorate a tree at Christmas.
Christmas is in winter.
I sang songs at Christmas.

more.def: A holiday on December 25 that Christians celebrate for the birth of Jesus, when many families also give gifts.
examples: Our family bakes cookies and gives gifts at Christmas.
Lights and wreaths decorate the town before Christmas.
We sang carols at the school concert near Christmas.
